summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of primary sclerosing cholangitis and cirrhosis was admitted for recurrent right upper quadrant pain and nausea, consistent with cholangitis. She had been started on doxycycline by her hepatologist without improvement. Initial labs showed mild abnormalities, and blood and urine cultures were negative. Imaging revealed a 5 mm obstructive stone in the common hepatic duct. She underwent ERCP with Spyglass cholangioscopy, during which an embedded stone was identified and partially removed using biopsies and balloon sweeps. She was treated with IV meropenem, transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin for completion at home, and showed clinical improvement. Her chronic conditions, including hypertension, hypothyroidism, GERD, and depression, were managed throughout. She was discharged home with a plan to complete antibiotics, resume rifaximin, and follow up with the liver center.
